findings.issue_text: [High/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side file size check now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so admin-configured limits (e.g. default `max_image_size_kb` of 4096KB) are no longer enforced client-side and users get a confusing server failure after passing the client check

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 ("entity too large") error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit, so the error message shown to users states the wrong maximum whenever the site setting differs

[High/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download path hardcodes `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so downloads via API bypass the configured size cap entirely (a site allowing only 2MB images will download up to 10MB from arbitrary URLs)

[Medium/bug] app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-155 — `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`resize` signatures changed from `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` to `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`; other callers still using the old 4-argument form will silently misbehave (old `max_height` lands in `opts`, producing e.g. `-resize 100x100` from width alone and dropping animation/other options) — either update all callers or keep the old signature as a wrapper

[Medium/performance] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — The downsize loop synchronously shells out to ImageMagick up to 5 times per upload on the request thread; each `80%` resize only cuts pixel count to ~64%, so a very large image can still exceed `max_image_size_kb` after 5 attempts and the oversized file is silently uploaded anyway — consider computing the required scale factor up front and/or failing gracefully when the loop is exhausted

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-68 — If `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (ImageMagick missing/misconfigured, corrupt image), the false return value of `convert_with` is ignored; the loop spins through all 5 attempts re-invoking a failing command and then uploads the original oversized file with no error surfaced — failures should break the loop early

[Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` trusts the filename/URL extension only; a non-image payload with an `.png` name (e.g. via API URL) will be fed to ImageMagick 5 times pointlessly on every request — image-type detection should use content/`FastImage` rather than extension

[Medium/test_gap] app/models/optimized_image.rb / app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb — No tests cover the new auto-downsize loop (boundary: file exactly at limit, non-image file, downsize failure, >5-attempt exhaustion) nor the `downsize`/`resize` signature change, which is the kind of refactor existing tests should have caught across all callers

[Low/doc_defect] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — The new auto-downsizing behavior silently alters users' uploaded images (up to ~67% pixel reduction after one pass) with no documentation or user-facing indication; site admins configuring `max_image_size_kb` are not told uploads will be silently degraded rather than rejected

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js`, the 413 handler was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). If the server-side limit (`SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`) is configured to something other than 10MB, the user-facing error message will report an incorrect maximum size.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download path hardcodes `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so downloads via API bypass the configured size cap entirely (a site allowing only 2MB images will download up to 10MB from arbitrary URLs)

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL download limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This means the configured site cap is no longer enforced at the download step for API-provided URLs, so a site with a smaller limit (e.g., 2MB) can still fetch up to 10MB from arbitrary URLs before any later processing/validation occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — The downsize loop synchronously shells out to ImageMagick up to 5 times per upload on the request thread; each `80%` resize only cuts pixel count to ~64%, so a very large image can still exceed `max_image_size_kb` after 5 attempts and the oversized file is silently uploaded anyway — consider computing the required scale factor up front and/or failing gracefully when the loop is exhausted

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`, which shells out via backticks in `OptimizedImage.convert_with` (request-thread work, potentially up to 5 ImageMagick invocations per upload). The loop also has no explicit handling for the case where `attempt` reaches 0 while `tempfile.size` remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; it will proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` regardless. Whether that results in a “silently uploaded oversized file” can’t be confirmed from this diff (depends on `Upload.create_for` validations), but the performance/edge-case concern is directly grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-68 — If `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (ImageMagick missing/misconfigured, corrupt image), the false return value of `convert_with` is ignored; the loop spins through all 5 attempts re-invoking a failing command and then uploads the original oversized file with no error surfaced — failures should break the loop early

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but does not check its return value; `OptimizedImage.convert_with` can return `false` on failure, so a persistent failure would indeed cause up to 5 redundant retries until `attempt` reaches 0. However, the finding’s claim that this necessarily results in uploading an oversized file “with no error surfaced” is not verifiable from the diff alone because `Upload.create_for(...)` may still enforce size limits and error out; that code isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` trusts the filename/URL extension only; a non-image payload with an `.png` name (e.g. via API URL) will be fed to ImageMagick 5 times pointlessly on every request — image-type detection should use content/`FastImage` rather than extension

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing block in `uploads_controller.rb` gates ImageMagick processing with `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and `filename` comes from the URL basename or uploaded filename in this diff. The diff does not show any content-based verification before calling `OptimizedImage.downsize`, so it’s plausible that a non-image payload named `*.png` could trigger up to 5 attempted downsizes (wasted work / robustness concern). However, whether `FileHelper.is_image?` is purely extension-based cannot be verified from the diff alone, and the loop appears to fail gracefully (no exception handling shown), so this is better framed as a non-bug review issue rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] app/models/optimized_image.rb / app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb — No tests cover the new auto-downsize loop (boundary: file exactly at limit, non-image file, downsize failure, >5-attempt exhaustion) nor the `downsize`/`resize` signature change, which is the kind of refactor existing tests should have caught across all callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload` (a 5-try loop that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` until under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`), and refactors `OptimizedImage` method signatures (`optimize` now takes a single `dimensions` argument; `resize`/`downsize` call sites change). The PR diff shows no accompanying tests for these new/changed code paths, and the edge cases called out (exact-limit boundary, non-image skipping via `FileHelper.is_image?`, failure to shrink, exhausting 5 attempts) are directly implied by the new loop/conditional logic. While we can’t prove from the diff that *no* existing tests cover this, the concern is specific and grounded in newly introduced/refactored logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — The new auto-downsizing behavior silently alters users' uploaded images (up to ~67% pixel reduction after one pass) with no documentation or user-facing indication; site admins configuring `max_image_size_kb` are not told uploads will be silently degraded rather than rejected

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a loop that downsizes oversized image uploads in-place before creating the Upload (uploads_controller.rb: new while loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`), and there is no user-facing message or indicator in this change that the file was modified rather than rejected. That’s a concrete UX/product-change concern grounded in the diff, but it appears intentional (comment: "allow users to upload large images...") rather than an outright correctness bug. The specific claim about "~67% pixel reduction" isn’t directly supported by the diff, but the broader point about silent alteration is.
